item.title: security: DeadLock ransomware: Breaking down a Rust-based encryptor with decentralized recovery infrastructure
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes DeadLock ransomware as a financially motivated operation using a Rust-based encryptor and decentralized infrastructure for victim communications, negotiations, and data leak operations. The group uses double extortion to pressure victims.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: CaptiveCrunch: Midnight Blizzard targets travelers worldwide for malware delivery and credential theft
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2945, a sub-cluster of Midnight Blizzard, has been compromising sign-in portals at hospitality organizations since May 2026 to deliver malware to travelers and steal credentials. The campaign is named CaptiveCrunch and targets travelers worldwide.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Rethinking security for the age of AI
item.description:
Microsoft says cybersecurity is changing in the AI era and introduces a new security cyber stack called Project Perception. The post frames this as a rethink of security architecture rather than a specific product release.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Securing our future: July 2026 progress report on Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative
item.description:
Microsoft published its July 2026 Secure Future Initiative progress report, summarizing work on secure foundations, AI-assisted defense, and broader cybersecurity readiness. The provided text is only a brief overview and does not include specific implementation details or metrics.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: AI brands as bait: How threat actors are using the AI hype in social engineering
item.description:
Threat actors are using AI-related brands and public interest in AI as social engineering lures. Microsoft says attackers are both operationalizing AI to speed up attacks and exploiting AI hype to make scams more convincing.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
